comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts a gripper’s threaded opening stop, locks the setting, and verifies retained motion; PR 2250 assembles a laryngoscope blade onto a hinge bar and opens it into a lit detent.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous hex-driver counterholding and thin-jam-nut tightening so lock torque does not disturb the stop, followed by tool withdrawal and actuation. PR 2250 requires slot-to-bar hook insertion, hinged swinging with regrasping, and detent engagement; it does not test coupled threaded adjustment or countertorque.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate scores target opening accuracy, seated/retained nuts, three repeatable cycles, limited stop drift, and released clearance. PR 2250 scores blade hook depth/alignment, at least 45° swing, 90° lit-detent engagement, tray placement, release, and one-second stillness, with off-table loss scoring zero. Both available PR 2250 spec versions agree; no material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: The shared ideas of articulated motion, final release, and functional checking are generic. The candidate’s defining tested ability is preserving a calibrated threaded stop while locking it against reaction torque and proving retention across cycles, whereas PR 2250 tests hook-on assembly and detent latching of two initially separate parts.
